title: B1 canonical snapshot and revision authority
description:
## Summary
Implement outside-handoff B1 so resolved generation snapshots and revision IDs derive from one detached canonical definition.

## User Mandate
> Carefully review the latest work and this external audit/task plan and implement the next set of tasks. Here is the prior agent's end report

STRICT. Binding constraints: use the 2026-09-05 post-PR1 outside handoff as the primary sprint reference; implement the next dependency-ready wave; preserve CreatureDefinition as authoring authority; keep generated data detached from later authored mutation; retain raw-definition overloads only at outer compatibility boundaries; record focused validation evidence; do not introduce a second snapshot architecture, generic service framework, generic SDF IR, or generic animation framework.

## Scope
- Canonicalize a detached input copy before snapshot resolution.
- Derive RevisionId from exactly that canonical input.
- Resolve all snapshot data from that same canonical input.
- Keep authoring DNA unmodified.
- Add focused canonical-equivalence and post-snapshot mutation regression coverage.
- Keep the existing resolved snapshot as the single runtime boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Canonicalization-equivalent definitions have equal revision IDs and equivalent resolved output.
- Mutating authored DNA after snapshot creation cannot mutate snapshot data or revision.
- Stable source identity and ordering remain preserved.
- Existing generation and compatibility overloads continue to work.
- Focused runtime build and Unity validation pass.

## Validation
Pending focused test, runtime build, Unity console inspection, and diff review.

## Findings
The current resolver computes the revision through serializer canonicalization but resolves morphology from the original definition. This can make revision authority and resolved data derive from different representations.

## Blockers
None known.

## Next Step
Update the resolver and add focused regression coverage, then record evidence before closing the task.

## Implementation Evidence
- Updated `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot.Resolve` to canonicalize a detached `CreatureDefinition` once and use that canonical input for revision hashing, body resolution, ordered parts, frame resolution, appearance, bounds, generation settings, forward, and symmetry.
- Changed revision hashing to write the already-canonical definition directly, avoiding a second canonicalization path.
- Extended `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot_CanonicalizationParity_MatchesCanonicalizedResolve` with quantization-sensitive position, rotation, and scale values.
- Preserved the existing snapshot type, raw-definition compatibility entry points, and authoritative authored DNA ownership.

## Validation Evidence
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore`: passed, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Focused Unity PlayMode test `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot_CanonicalizationParity_MatchesCanonicalizedResolve`: 1/1 passed.
- Full Unity PlayMode assembly `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime`: 466/466 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Unity console after focused and full runs: no product errors or warnings; only test-result and cleanup logs.
- `dotnet build CreatureCreator.slnx --no-restore`: passed, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `git diff --check`: passed; only existing line-ending normalization warnings were reported.

## Findings
The original resolver hashed serializer-canonicalized data but resolved morphology from the authored definition. B1 now gives revision and resolved output one canonical source of truth while leaving the authored definition unmodified.

## Residual Risk
Unity editor EditMode tests were not rerun because this slice changes runtime snapshot resolution only. Existing unrelated worktree changes remain untouched and are outside TSK-0112.
